text: Subscribe to skip adsAdvertisementPsychologyEven Dogs Seem to Experience the Mysterious Bouba/Kiki EffectBut why?JCBy Jake Currie5:00 PM CDT on October 15, 2026Add Nautilus to GoogleThe bouba/kiki effect is one of the odder psychological phenomena. For some reason, when presented with two random shapes (one angular and another rounded), and two nonsense words (“kiki” and “bouba”), people tend to associate bouba with the lobed figure and kiki with the spiky one. First discovered in the 1920s, this particular idiosyncrasy of the human mind is a strong indication that we associate certain sounds with certain shapes, which has important implications for the evolution of language.  Kiki and bouba, I think you can guess which is which. Credit: Adobe StockIt’s also proved to be strikingly widespread. Cultures from around the globe speaking different languages can “correctly” identify bouba and kiki (including those with no written language). In fact, when people who have been blind since birth are presented with 3D representations of the figures, they too get it right. Now, according to a new study published in the Proceedings of the Royal Society B: Biological Sciences, the bouba/kiki effect may even extend to dogs.Subscribe to skip adsAdvertisement
